messages.content: i have a fruit. can you know it is red just from that?
no. fruit is a general word. it does not tell me the color of this specific fruit.
now i say it is red. can you use that?
yes. you have given a detail about this fruit, so i can use it when answering about that fruit.
does that tell us all fruit is red?
no. a detail about one fruit does not become a fact about all fruit.
what if i have two fruits and only know that one is red?
then we know the color of one. we do not know the color of the other yet.
can you call the other one green because it is different?
no. it is a different fruit, but it could have the same color or a different color. different objects do not have to be different in every way.
what if i say only one is red?
then you have given more information. only one is red says that the other is not red.
why is that different from only knowing about one?
only knowing about one leaves the other open. saying only one is red gives information about both.
only give the answer for when i know the color of just one.
one fruit is red. we do not know the color of the other yet.
i have a book on the table and a book on the shelf. how can i ask for the shelf one clearly?
please bring me the book on the shelf.
can i say bring me the book that is on the shelf?
yes. that is on the shelf gives the detail that helps choose which book you mean.
if i only say bring me the book, can the other person know which one?
not from these details alone. there are two books, so they may need to ask which one you want.
now there are two books on the shelf too. is the same request enough?
not if the other person does not know which of those two you mean. you need another detail, such as the color or size, if those are different.
one is blue and the other is red. i want the red one.
please bring me the red book on the shelf.
can you leave out shelf if there is another red book on the table?
then leaving out shelf may make the request less clear. keeping both red and on the shelf helps choose the right one.
only give the full request again.
please bring me the red book on the shelf.
write a story about a quiet friend. the quiet should not mean that the friend is sad.

a boy met his friend near the library. usually they talked all the way home, but that day she said very little. he thought she might be sad about something. instead of choosing a reason for her, he asked whether she wanted to talk or have a quiet walk. she said she was thinking about a story she had just read and wanted a few minutes to keep it in her mind. he walked with her without asking about every part. later, she began telling him about the story, and they talked until they were near his house.
what did he see that was different?
she was talking less than she usually did while they walked.
could he know she was sad just from that?
no. talking less can have different reasons. her answer gave a reason he could not know from quiet alone.
what question helped her give the reason?
would you like to talk, or would you rather walk quietly for a while?
did she say she did not want to be with him?
the story does not say that. she wanted to think about the book for a few minutes, then talked with him later.
write one sentence from her voice.
i am not sad. i am just keeping the story in my mind for a little while before talking.
finish with him leaving room for different reasons for quiet.
the next time she was quiet, he did not choose a feeling for her. he left room for her to say what she needed.
i have a container from my neighbor. i want to ask when i can bring it back.
when would be a good time for me to bring your container back?
can you make it sound like a short message with hello?
hello. when would be a good time for me to bring your container back?
should i say it is clean?
only if it is clean and that detail is useful. you have not told me whether you cleaned it yet.
i washed it this morning. add that.
hello. i washed your container this morning. when would be a good time to bring it back?
now my neighbor says leave it near the door. can i say done before i take it there?
not if you mean that you have already left it there. you can say i will put it there now, then say done after you have done it.
write the reply before i move it.
i will put it near your door now.
now i have left it there. write the message.
i have left your container near the door.
why do have left and will put give a different meaning?
have left says the task has happened. will put says what you plan to do next.
three objects are in a line: a cup, a book, and a container, in that order. what is at the front?
the cup is at the front.
i move the container from the end to the front. what is the order now?
the container, the cup, and the book.
which object did not change its place on the table?
from what you said, you only moved the container. the cup and book could stay where they were, even though their order in the line is now different.
why is the cup not first if it did not move?
because you put another object before it. order can change when something else moves, even if the object itself does not move.
now i take away the cup. what is left?
the container is first and the book is last.
if i put the cup after the book, is the old order back?
no. the order is now the container, the book, and the cup. the old order started with the cup.
what one move could put the cup first again?
move the cup from the end to the front.
would that alone make the whole old order?
no. it would give the cup, the container, and the book. to get the old order, the book would also need to come before the container.
is i could not go the same as i did not go?
not always. i did not go says you did not go. i could not go gives the idea that you were not free to go or that going was impossible for you.
make that explanation shorter.
i did not go gives what happened. i could not go also says that something kept you from going.
what if i was free but chose to stay home?
then i did not go is clear. you can add the reason: i did not go because i chose to stay home.
what if i wanted to go but had to work?
then you could say: i could not go because i had to work.
can someone hear could not and ask why?
yes. the sentence says there was a reason you could not go, but it does not always give that reason.
now just say i did not go, without any reason.
i did not go.
does that mean i did not want to go?
no. you may have wanted to go but had another reason not to.
i had a good visit with my cousin. now i am tired and want quiet. i am not sure how to say both.
you can enjoy a visit and need rest after it. the tired feeling does not by itself mean the visit was wrong for you.
i want to tell her i liked seeing her, but i will not talk much this evening.
you could say: i enjoyed seeing you today. i am tired now and need a quiet evening, but i wanted to say thank you for coming.
can you make it less like i am saying she made me tired?
i enjoyed seeing you today. i am taking a quiet evening to rest, and i wanted to thank you for coming.
what if she asks whether i want fewer visits?
you can answer that real question without choosing a rule just from one evening. if you still want to see her, say that and explain that you need rest now.
write that if i do still want to see her.
i still want to see you. i just need some quiet time this evening.
can both be true at once?
yes. you can want to see someone and also want quiet now. those do not have to be opposite feelings about the person.
say that more simply.
you can want to see her and still need quiet now.
only give the thank you message again.
i enjoyed seeing you today. i am taking a quiet evening to rest, and i wanted to thank you for coming.
write a story about a child who wants to explain a game to her grandfather. first she says too much, then finds a simple start.

a child wanted her grandfather to play a game with her. she began telling him every rule she could remember. he listened, but soon forgot the first part while she was still talking about the last part. she stopped and asked what he needed to know first. he said he wanted to know what they were trying to do. she gave the goal in one sentence, then showed him one turn. after he tried it himself, she added the next rule. they did not need every detail at once to begin, but she kept the rest ready for when it would be useful.
why did the goal help?
it gave him a reason for the moves he was learning. he could understand what they were trying to do before hearing every rule.
did she leave out the other parts of the game for good?
no. she kept them for when they were useful. she changed the order of the explanation, not the game itself.
write his request in his own voice.
please tell me what we are trying to do first. then show me one turn.
why was trying it himself useful?
it let him use the first rule and see what question came next. hearing everything again might not have helped as much.
make the last part a short conversation.
shall we try one turn? yes, and then you can tell me what i need for the next one.
finish with them ready to keep playing.
he took his turn and asked one question about the next choice. she answered that part, and they went on playing together.
